best_lineage.idea: Replace the O(n log n) merge sort with a hybrid that uses LSD Radix Sort for large inputs (fast on random and duplicate-heavy data) and Introsort (with insertion sort) for small inputs, drastically improving throughput on the "uniform" and "dups1000" distributions where the current merge sort is slow.

The current LSD Radix Sort uses 4 passes of 8-bit histograms, which incurs high overhead on sorted/reverse-sorted data due to 4 full memory scans and allocations; switching to 3 passes of 11-bit histograms reduces passes by 25%, improves cache locality, and naturally handles the "many duplicates" case better, while raising the threshold ensures small inputs use the highly optimized introsort.
